title: Regional evacuation crediting and prioritized load redistribution
creator: Avery Chen
description: Define a policy and operational runbook for evacuating traffic from degraded regions while preserving customer SLO guarantees through an evacuation crediting mechanism and prioritized load redistribution. This ticket formalizes the SLO-to-evacuation-credit mapping, per-model transfer rules, and the circuit-breaker thresholds that trigger staged load shedding and rerouting.
background: We frequently run into partial regional degradation where one cloud region has constrained capacity or elevated tail latency for specific model variants. Current behavior has been ad-hoc: manual reroutes or blunt throttles that either over-burst costs or cause unexpected customer degradations. We need a formal, reproducible policy that: (1) defines how to momentarily borrow capacity/quality allowances between regions without violating tenant contracts, (2) specifies prioritized redistribution so high-priority tenants keep access, and (3) integrates with circuit breakers to automate safe rollback.
goals: 1) Create a deterministic mapping from SLO error-budget burn to evac-credits that can be transferred between regions. 2) Define a prioritized redistribution algorithm that respects tenant tier, pinned variants, and token-weighted fairness. 3) Provide concrete circuit-breaker thresholds and stepwise runbook to automate evacuation and rebalancing. 4) Offer simulation examples and alerting queries for operations.
non_goals: 1) Replacing existing multi-region routing infra (this ticket builds on top of the routing layer). 2) Designing a new billing primitive. 3) Handling long-term capacity planning decisions.
proposed_policy: Overview: When a region R reports sustained SLI degradation (tail latency or availability) beyond a configurable threshold, the system will enter a staged evacuation: 1) Soft migration (prefix reroute + shadowing) 2) Evac-credit allocation and prioritized redistribution 3) Hard diversion with circuit-breaker enforcement. Evac-credits: Each region maintains an evac-credit balance per model-variant. Credits are minted when the local region is underutilized relative to target SLO headroom and are consumed when absorbing traffic from remote evacuees. Transfer rules: - Credits are transferred atomically per model-variant and tenant-route. - Transfers are capped by a per-tenant escrow (default 15% of monthly token allocation) unless tenant opts in to higher borrowing. Prioritization: Incoming evacuees are scored by (tenant_tier_weight * urgency_factor * quality_sensitivity). High-priority tenants (enterprise) are offered first slots up to their pre-declared guarantees. Quality degradation windows: A decaying quality allowance is applied (e.g., 10% quality reduction permissible for 30 minutes, then 5% for next 60 minutes), encoded as token-quality multipliers. Circuit breaker integration: Circuit breaker trips when regional 95th tail latency > SLO threshold * 1.5 for 2 consecutive minutes OR error budget burn rate > 20x for 5 minutes. On trip: mark region degraded, start evacuation stage 2. On sustained recovery metrics, unwind credits and return traffic per rollout plan.
formula_examples: 1) Evac-credit mint: credit_minutes = floor(available_headroom_tokens / expected_tps) * 60. Example: available_headroom_tokens=120k tokens/hr, expected_tps=10 requests/sec ~ 36k tokens/hr -> credit_minutes = floor(120k/36k)*60 = 3*60 = 180 minutes. 2) Transfer cap: transfer_cap_tokens = min(tenant_escrow_tokens, region_credit_tokens*0.3). 3) Priority score = tenant_tier_weight * (1 + severity_score) * (1 - model_quality_penalty). Example weights: enterprise=1.2, standard=1.0, free=0.7. severity_score normalized 0..1 based on observed latency delta.
metrics_and_slis: Primary SLIs: - availability.success_rate (1 - error_rate) per endpoint/model per region - latency.p95_ms and latency.p99_ms per endpoint/model per region Secondary SLIs: - quality.regression_rate (promptset-based) - throughput.tokens_per_second Observability: - Expose evac_credit_{region,model} gauge - Expose evac_inbound_flow_{tenant,region} counter SLO declarations: - Endpoint X: availability >= 99.9% monthly, p95 <= 300ms. Error budget accounting: - When traffic is absorbed by a remote region and a small quality reduction policy applies, account consumption to the origin region's error budget first; if origin budget exhausted, debit a transient borrowed credit from destination's evac balance and mark for reconciliation.
runbook_summary: Staged response: 1) Detect: Alert fires when p95 > threshold or error budget burn rate high. 2) Observe: Run preflight query to sample request/response sizes and token distribution. 3) Soft migration: enable prefix reroutes for non-critical routes and start shadow traffic to candidate regions. 4) Allocate evac-credits: compute transfer cap, notify tenants with affected contracts (automated message). 5) Prioritized redistribution: accept traffic according to priority score until evac-credit depleted. 6) Hard diversion: if degradation persists and credits are consumed, enable circuit-breaker reroute for lower-priority tenants and apply rate caps. 7) Recovery: monitor p95/p99 and wind down in reverse order, reconcile credits, produce postmortem within 72 hours.
rollback_criteria: Immediate rollback (re-route back to origin) if: - p95 in origin improves to <= SLO threshold for 10 continuous minutes AND - error budget burn rate falls below 2x baseline for 30 minutes AND - no new infra incidents reported. Abort ongoing hard diversion and re-enable normal routing.
telemetry_queries: 1) Identify degradation window: SELECT region, model, percentile(95, latency_ms) FROM requests WHERE timestamp >= now() - 10m GROUP BY region, model; 2) Credit balance: SELECT sum(evac_credit_minutes) FROM evac_credits WHERE region='R' AND model='M'; 3) Inbound flow by tenant: SELECT tenant, sum(tokens) FROM requests WHERE dest_region='R2' AND origin_region='R1' AND timestamp >= now()-1h GROUP BY tenant; 4) Error budget burn: SELECT rolling_burn_rate FROM error_budget WHERE endpoint='E' AND region='R'
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): implement evac-credit bookkeeping and read-only dashboards in staging, simulate 5 failure scenarios with synthetic load (2 weeks). Phase 2 (pilot): enable soft migration and prioritized redistribution for a single low-risk customer cohort (4 weeks). Phase 3 (region-wide): enable automated credit transfers + circuit-breaker enforcement for non-production clusters, monitor for 2 weeks. Phase 4 (GA): enable full policy for production regions with expanded alerting and documented tenant opt-in paths. Post-GA: automate reconciliation reports and billing-safe audit logs.
open_questions: 1) Should evac-credit transfer be visible on tenant billing pages or hidden until reconciliation? 2) What is the default tenant_escrow limit (15% is provisional)? 3) Should we allow cross-model crediting for compatible variants, or restrict transfers strictly by variant? 4) Are QA promptsets for quality-regression detection sufficient to gate redistribution?
acceptance_criteria: 1) Evac-credit gauge emitted for all regions and models in staging. 2) Simulation harness can trigger staged evacuation and verify credits decrement and re-increment on unwind. 3) Circuit-breaker trips at configured thresholds and triggers prioritized redistribution. 4) Documentation (Confluence) and an operations runbook present with play-by-play steps and sample alerts. 5) Two run simulations executed and results reviewed by SRE and Product.
notes: This design intentionally separates short-term borrowed capacity (evac-credits) from long-term billing adjustments. Reconciliation and billing policy will be handled in a follow-up ticket. Coordinate with customer success for tenant opt-in messaging and with legal for potential contract exceptions.
postmortem_requirements: Any GA-triggered evacuation that affects >5% of production tenants or lasts >60 minutes requires a postmortem within 72 hours containing: incident timeline, credit accounting, customer impact summary, and recommended mitigations.
estimated_cost_impact: Initial implementation mostly infra and SRE effort; anticipated cloud egress and cross-region token costs during pilot are estimated at $8k-$20k depending on traffic patterns. Production tuning expected to reduce run costs by avoiding aggressive failovers.
implementation_notes: - Use existing routing decision service extension points for prefix reroute and tenant-tier scoring. - Add evac_credit tables to telemetry store with TTL-based decay. - Expose a debug endpoint to simulate credit transfers for test harness. - Include guardrails to prevent cascading credit drains (circuit-breaker threshold per-region-global cap).
